title: StockSmart Replenishment Planning Standard — Customer-Owned Reorder Point of a Converted Bin
content:
The StockSmart Vendor-Managed Inventory Program sets the customer-owned reorder point of a bin whose slow-moving consigned item was withdrawn at a par review as follows.

**§1 The converted item.** The converted item is the item of the program's most recent consignment withdrawal; where two or more consignment withdrawals carry that most recent date, or there is none, no conversion reorder point is set under this standard. A consignment withdrawal counts as a par-review conversion only where the converted item's bin carries no removal entry and the program is not closed; after a withdrawal that follows the removal of the bin or the end of the program, no conversion reorder point is set under this standard. The bin's entries of their latest date are the entries of the item's bin that carry the most recent effective date among them.

**§2 Window.** A row's age in whole months is the number of calendar months from its date to today, less one when today's day of the month is earlier than the row's day of the month; the last twelve months hold rows of age below twelve.

**§3 Inputs.** The daily draw of the converted item is its consumption billed over the last twelve months divided by 365, and the standard days are the visit gap, 30 days divided by the visits the program's tier schedules a month (7 days for a tier scheduling none), plus the tier's replenishment lead business days counted as days. No further lead days are added (0 days), no safety units are added (0 units) and the value share is the whole, 1.

**§4 The reorder point.** The conversion reorder point is worked out in this order: the daily draw is multiplied by the lead time in days, which is the standard days plus every further lead day added; the safety units are added to that product; and the sum is multiplied by the value share, taken to six decimal places and rounded up to the next whole unit.

### Worked figures (hypothetical items and tiers)

| Consumption, last twelve months | Daily draw | Tier visits a month; lead business days | Standard days | Product to six decimals | Reorder point |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 365 units | 1.000000 | 4; 1 | 7.5 plus 1 is 8.5 | 8.500000 | 9 |
| 730 units | 2.000000 | none; 2 | 7 plus 2 is 9 | 18.000000 | 18 |
| 100 units | 0.273973 | 2; 1 | 15 plus 1 is 16 | 4.383562 | 5 |

The order in §4 is fixed: the multiplication by the value share acts on the whole sum of the lead-time demand and the safety units, and the rounding up comes last.
